rules.title: MR1 · Recover degraded land
rules.description: Seed-grown carob in favourable rootable and moisture pockets; irregular mixed groups and retained open ground.
rules.limitations: Illustrative planning guidance, not a verified site prescription.

rules.title: MR2 · Rainfall capture
rules.description: Conceptual planting islands, donor catchment and safe overflow. MR1 and MR2 can be combined.
rules.limitations: Illustrative planning guidance, not a verified site prescription.

rules.title: Assumed moisture pocket
rules.description: An assumed pocket offers a conditional encina suggestion at the editable species density. Its first automatically positioned example follows the pocket. Additional individuals are layout examples, not verified moist microsites. Pocket size does not establish water availability or oak suitability.
rules.limitations: Illustrative planning guidance, not a verified site prescription.

rules.title: Stone surface mulch
rules.description: Surface stone cover around selected plants; not a buried drainage layer. Ring dimensions are project assumptions.
rules.limitations: Illustrative planning guidance, not a verified site prescription.

rules.title: Density and area basis
rules.description: Pies/ha means individual trees or stems per hectare. MR1 passages give <350, <100 and <200 in different contexts: no single target is inferred. Whole-zone density differs from spacing within groups; carob, total trees and shrubs are separate.
rules.limitations: Illustrative planning guidance, not a verified site prescription.

rules.title: Planting season and stock
rules.description: For limited-care restoration plant in autumn and avoid delays, especially on shallow or stony soils. Una savia means one growing season (1+0); >200 cm³ is >0.2 L. Table 5.14 gives November–March and 200–300 cm³; these contexts differ. Larger stock is not automatically better.
rules.limitations: Illustrative planning guidance, not a verified site prescription.

rules.title: Reported Almería survival
rules.description: The handbook reports 40–60% carob survival in Almería (Planelles et al., 2001), without a monitoring period here. Historical evidence, not an annual probability or a forecast for this zone.
rules.limitations: Illustrative planning guidance, not a verified site prescription.

rules.title: Low-maintenance protective restoration
rules.description: Routine field fertilizer, formation pruning and continuing competition control are generally omitted. Table 5.14 also lists establishment weeding. This is a protective-management baseline, not proof of maximum growth or zero establishment water.
rules.limitations: Illustrative planning guidance, not a verified site prescription.

rules.title: Illustrative geometry and layout clearance
rules.description: Generated coordinates, layout clearances, moisture-pocket and mulch geometry are editable project assumptions. Root-ball and mature-crown overlays are separate, evidence-qualified dimensions; they do not establish planting spacing.
rules.limitations: No source supplies these exact generated coordinates or universally optimal quantities.

rules.title: Oak and companion context
rules.description: Coscoja is usually a shrub; its natural occurrence near 200 mm annual rainfall at Cabo de Gata is not a seedling survival guarantee. Encina is a conditional larger-tree candidate for favourable soil/moisture pockets. Cork oak needs suitable soil chemistry and moisture; myrtle is a moisture-pocket candidate. Phillyrea angustifolia and P. latifolia are distinct taxa. A vegetation series describes reference communities and related stages, not a mandatory planting mix or a guarantee of tall forest.
rules.limitations: No series or species suitability is assigned to this assumed zone. Rainfall alone is insufficient.

rules.title: Editable density scenarios
rules.description: Carob starts at 350/ha and other species at 50/ha. These are project assumptions, not handbook recommendations. Counts use whole-zone area and round halves upward. At 200 square metres, 350/ha gives seven plants.
rules.limitations: 350 equals, and does not satisfy, the strict <350 passage. The <100 and <200 passages have different contexts; no suitability cap is inferred.

rules.title: Root balls and indicative mature spread
rules.description: Root-ball dimensions depend on supplied nursery stock. Mature crown ranges are context-qualified references, never growth or root-spread forecasts. Unknown dimensions remain unknown.
rules.limitations: Container volume does not establish width. Garden spread ranges do not predict dryland restoration performance.

rules.title: Shared illustrative nursery root ball
rules.description: Use the configured shared root-ball drawing diameter (12 cm initially) where no explicit user dimension or documented stock width is available. This user-selected visual assumption applies to catalogue and custom plants.
rules.limitations: The book discusses small forestry cells and 1–2 L stock but does not establish this 12 cm value. It has no effect on costs, layout clearance, spacing or planting-hole recommendations; entered dimensions take precedence.

vegetation_combinations.title: Warm lentisco series · Bupleuro–Pistacieto
vegetation_combinations.description: Vegetation-series reference, not a compulsory mixture. FOREST-003 calls it a coscoja series although the Latin name identifies lentisco: the source conflict is retained. Optional members are illustrative companions, not a complete association.
